topic: Barehands: Webcam-Powered Hand Tracking to Control Your Screen

key_points: The canonical open-source project: webcam turns into a hand-tracked interface for AI — no headset, no controllers, no gloves.
Run it with `git clone` + `python3 server.py` (stdlib only; Windows uses run.bat) then open http://127.0.0.1:8794/stage.html in Chrome and allow the camera.
Hand tracking via Google MediaPipe (Apache 2.0), 3D rendering via three.js (MIT), both loaded from CDNs on first run.

Gestures: tap (quick pinch) to open/close, pinch-drag to move, rotate while holding still, two-hand scale, flick to throw, clap to clear the board, and 'the claw' to pull distant objects through the air.
It has no AI built in — it is a 'body': wire any AI in as the brain via tiny files in state/ (the ring is a face) and bin/board.sh + bin/board-state.sh (the board is a stage).
Vault is just a folder of markdown, so an Obsidian vault works as-is; only files inside media/ ever appear on the board (a safety jail).
Licensed AGPL-3.0 — free to use and modify commercially; must stay open if redistributed.
Google's official Hand Landmarker model detects 21 hand-knuckle landmarks inside detected hand regions.
Trained on ~30K real-world images plus synthetic rendered hand models; ships as a bundle of a palm detection model + a hand landmark model.
Supports live-stream, video, and image modes with configurable confidence thresholds (hand presence, palm detection).
The underlying tech that makes barehands-style browser hand tracking possible without custom hardware.
Academic competitor: turns a standard webcam into a fully functional virtual mouse for the entire OS.
Leverages YOLOv26 single-stage object detection plus a 21-landmark hand pose estimation model.
Goal is bare-hand gesture control of the OS with no physical mouse or touchpad — the same 'hands instead of input devices' premise as barehands.
Companion project (~756 stars) that installs the whole jaredrhod stack — memory, voice, face, and hands — in one wizard.
Shows the ecosystem angle: barehands is the 'hands' component of a fuller local AI-agent setup.
Users can pick only the pieces they want, demonstrating how hand-tracked control fits into a broader personal-AI workflow.
Companion repo (~634 stars) that turns an Obsidian vault into an AI's working memory using plain markdown — no vector DB.
The vault it builds becomes a notes orb on the barehands board, connecting persistent memory to touchless screen control.
Illustrates the practical hook: pair the visual 'body' with an actual brain that remembers your work.
Search landscape for 'barehands hand tracking' is dominated by the jaredrhod/barehands repo and its forks (jarvis-barehands, nia-bare-hands, xgaisystems forks).
Indicates high but niche interest concentrated in the open-source/AI-agent builder community rather than broad consumer SEO.
Opportunity: few general tutorials exist that explain setup, gestures, and AI wiring in plain language.

stats.fact: jaredrhod/barehands has ~907 GitHub stars and ~199 forks, described as 'a webcam-powered, hand-tracked interface for your AI' (AGPL-3.0).
Google's MediaPipe project (the hand-tracking engine barehands uses) has ~36,868 stars and is the platform for cross-platform live ML solutions.
MediaPipe Hand Landmarker detects 21 hand-knuckle landmarks and was trained on approximately 30K real-world images plus synthetic rendered hand models.
Companion projects ship in the same ecosystem: fullstack-agent (~756 stars) and ai-memory-vault (~634 stars), forming a complete local AI-agent + touchless-interface stack.
barehands runs entirely on localhost with stdlib Python (python3 server.py) and loads MediaPipe + three.js from CDNs on first run — no install, no GPU required.
Gesture threshold calibration uses hand-shape ratios, not absolute size, so the same gesture gates work at any camera distance; a debug overlay and pose sampler ship for tuning.
The board is a 'stage' any program can drive: anything that can write a file or curl localhost can be the brain — Claude, a local LLM, a cron job, or a Stream Deck button.

angles: The 'no headset, no controllers, no gloves' angle — bare hands and a webcam instead of a VR/MR setup, with AGPL commercial-friendliness as a differentiator.
The AI-as-body metaphor: barehands is a 'body' with no brain — wire in Claude Code or any LLM via state/ files and bin/ scripts for true touchless AI-agent control.
Obsidian vault integration: any folder of markdown (including an existing Obsidian vault) becomes a touchable notes orb — practical for productivity users.
Local-first / privacy angle: everything runs on localhost, nothing leaves the machine, no cloud upload for hands or notes.
Gesture catalogue as the hook: tap, pinch-drag, throw, two-hand scale, clap-to-clear, and the 'claw' are novel enough to drive curiosity and demos.
Creator/community momentum: YouTube series, Discord builder community, forks showing real adoption in the AI-agent builder niche.
